orchestrator_output.text_narration: Magnets are objects that produce a magnetic field and attract materials like iron, nickel, and cobalt. Based on how they are made and how long they keep their magnetic power, magnets are classified into different types. First, magnets are divided into Natural and Artificial magnets. Natural magnets, like Magnetite, are found directly in nature but have weak magnetic power. Artificial magnets are human-made using metals like iron and steel, and they are much stronger. Second, artificial magnets can be Permanent or Temporary. Permanent magnets keep their magnetic property for a long time, like the magnets on refrigerator doors. Temporary magnets act like magnets only when placed near a strong magnetic field or when electric current flows through them. Artificial magnets come in many shapes for different uses. The Bar Magnet is a simple rectangular strip. The Horseshoe Magnet is U-shaped and brings both north and south poles closer together. We also have Cylindrical, Ring, and Button magnets used in toys, speakers, and compasses.
